references.text: Jesus withdraws to the mountain completely alone after receiving the kingdom, which contrasts with him going up on the mountain in verse 3 to sit with the disciples.
Jesus goes up on the mountain to be alone and pray. This shares the motif of the mountaintop in John 6:3, but with an opposite purpose (solitude/prayer versus teaching/fellowship with the disciples).
Jesus goes up on the mountain to be alone and pray. This shares the motif of the mountaintop in John 6:3, but with an opposite purpose (solitude/prayer versus teaching/fellowship with the disciples).
Jesus takes his disciples up on the mountain to pray. This shares the motif of the mountaintop in John 6:3, but with a different purpose (prayer versus teaching).
Moses goes up on Mount Sinai to meet the Lord. This shares the motif with Jesus going up on the mountain in John 6:3, but with a different purpose (meeting God versus teaching the disciples).
